name: Driving school
description: A driving school: upcoming course dates, a price list, the instructors and students' questions, with facts about licence categories, prices, vehicles and exams.

questions.question: Which licence categories do you teach?
questions.help: For example "B, B automatic, A1, A2".

questions.question: What does the cheapest course cost?
questions.help: An amount with the currency; the price list holds every variant and what it includes.

questions.question: What is the registration number of your driving school?
questions.help: The number of the licence or registration under which you may train drivers – check whether your law requires it on the site.

questions.question: Which vehicles do students learn in?
When and how do the theory lessons take place?
questions.help: For example "Tuesday and Thursday 17:00 in the classroom, or online at your own pace".

questions.question: Where do the exams take place?
Since which year has the school been teaching?

audit.message: Say which licence categories you teach – it is the first thing a student checks.
State the price of the course from – students compare schools by price.
Add the next course dates – students look for when the next course starts.
The price list has not changed for a year – check the course prices and the fees for extra lessons.
Fill in your phone number in Business details – students and parents call to ask about the next course.

claude: Students and their parents want to know which categories the school teaches, when the next course starts, what it costs and in what cars they will drive – put the next course dates, the price from and the categories on the home page and keep them as facts and courses, never as loose text that goes stale. Write plainly and encouragingly, without pressure. Never invent pass rates, the number of students trained, instructors, vehicles, prices or reviews, and do not promise a licence within a time or a first-time pass – training and exam rules are set by law and differ by country, so point out that the details should be checked with the owner. Each course date is one item in the courses collection; a course that has started drops out of the list by itself, so the list stays honest.
